Overview: Psoriasis is a life-long inflammatory autoimmune skin disorder that can involve the skin, nails, and joints, classified by the World Health Organization as a chronic, painful, disabling non-communicable disease. It is the most common type, accounting for over 80% of cases and presenting as well-demarcated, erythematous plaques with characteristic silvery, micaceous scales, typically on extensor surfaces like elbows, knees, and the scalp. The pathophysiology of psoriasis involves a complex interplay of aberrant immune responses and defective keratinocyte pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly aberrant Th1 and Th17 responses, and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-17, IL-23, and TNF-, which drive the inflammatory milieu within the epidermal layers.
Symptoms: Psoriasis symptoms vary depending on the type and location of the disease. Plaque psoriasis is the most common form of psoriasis. Other forms of psoriasis present with different symptoms. Nail psoriasis is particularly challenging to treat and significantly impacts quality-of-life and systemic comorbidities
Causes: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease involving a complex interplay between genetic and environmental factors
Preventions: **Lifestyle Modifications:** **Smoking cessation:** Excessive alcohol consumption can exacerbate psoriasis . **Alcohol moderation:** Excessive alcohol consumption can exacerbate psoriasis . **Infection control: **Prompt treatment of infections, especially streptococcal infections, can prevent flares, particularly guttate psoriasis
When to See a Doctor: Consult a dermatologist immediately if you have psoriasis.
